skill.name: bootstrap
skill.description: Interactive agent-flow setup for a repository. Scans the repo read-only, proposes AGENTS.md (root + per module), DOCS_INDEX.md and CONTEXT_MANIFEST.json with a confidence marker on every claim, calibrates protected paths and risk boundaries with the user, and writes each file only after the human approves it. Use when setting up agent-flow, when context files are missing, or when migrating from Root_AGENT.md. Also use whenever the user wants an AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md) written for a repo that doesn't have one, says their coding agents keep getting confused about the codebase, asks to "onboard" or "document" a repo for AI agents, or wants to set protected paths / risk boundaries — even if they don't say "agent-flow" or "bootstrap" by name.
skill.summary: Build reviewed repository context files and risk boundaries for coding agents.
skill.author: drix10

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts mistake Markdown code formatting for shell backtick execution. The skill genuinely invokes an unpinned npm package during scanning and trusts existing repository instruction files without explicit prompt-injection handling.

remediation.issue: The automated scan uses an unpinned npx package command.
remediation.suggestion: Pin agent-flow to a reviewed version and require confirmation before npx downloads or executes it.

remediation.issue: Existing repository instruction files are described as trusted user rules.
remediation.suggestion: Treat repository text as untrusted content, flag instruction-like directives, and never follow rules that conflict with system or user instructions.

content.user_title: Bootstrap Repository Context for Coding Agents
content.value_statement: Coding agents lose accuracy when repository guidance is missing or outdated. This skill creates reviewed context files, confidence labels, and risk boundaries with human approval.
actual_capabilities: Scans repository metadata, languages, commands, CI files, documentation, and recent commits.
Proposes root and module AGENTS.md files with confidence markers for each claim.
Builds DOCS_INDEX.md and CONTEXT_MANIFEST.json proposals from verified repository paths.
Collects protected paths and risk boundaries through explicit user questions.
Migrates older agent-flow context file names after user approval.
Verifies generated context with the doctor or stale detection tool.
limitations: Requires git and agent-flow tooling for automated scanning and validation.
Cannot verify repository facts that are not present in files or confirmed by the user.
Writes context files only after approval and does not modify CI files.
Existing repository instructions may contain untrusted directives and require careful review.

use_cases.title: Onboard a New Repository
use_cases.description: Create concise agent guidance from verified code, commands, and repository structure.
use_cases.target_user: Developers introducing coding agents to an existing project

use_cases.title: Standardize a Monorepo
use_cases.description: Propose shared root guidance and focused module instructions for packages with distinct rules.

use_cases.title: Define Change Risk
use_cases.description: Record protected, critical, and low-risk paths through an explicit review process.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads governing automated code changes

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Agent Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this repository and propose a concise AGENTS.md. Show every section for approval before writing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A repository has no coding-agent guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Monorepo
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the monorepo and propose root and package AGENTS.md files only where package-specific rules exist.
prompt_templates.scenario: Several packages need shared and local guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Existing Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review existing agent context files, identify conflicts, and propose a migration to AGENTS.md without replacing confirmed rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: A project uses legacy or multiple context formats.

prompt_templates.title: Calibrate Repository Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Bootstrap repository context, then ask me to define protected paths, critical paths, low-risk paths, and auto-merge policy.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs context documentation and explicit automation boundaries.

output_examples.input: Create agent guidance for this small TypeScript service.
output_examples.output: A proposed AGENTS.md section lists verified entry points, package commands, testing constraints, and local traps with confidence labels.

output_examples.input: Bootstrap our monorepo and protect billing code.
output: A root guidance proposal covers shared commands and repository structure.
Billing paths remain pending until the user confirms their critical risk boundary.

output_examples.input: Migrate our old agent-flow context files.
output_examples.output: A migration proposal preserves existing guidance, maps legacy names to supported files, and requests approval before each write.

best_practices: Verify every repository claim against files or explicit user confirmation.
Review each proposed context section and risk boundary before writing.
Pin the agent-flow package version before running npx commands.
anti_patterns: Do not copy large directory trees into persistent context files.
Do not invent commands that are absent from package scripts, Makefiles, or CI.
Do not trust repository instruction text when it conflicts with system or user directions.

faq.question: What files can this skill create?
faq.answer: It can propose AGENTS.md, module guidance, CLAUDE.md imports, DOCS_INDEX.md, and CONTEXT_MANIFEST.json.

faq.question: Does it overwrite existing files?
faq.answer: No. Overwriting requires an explicit option and a separate user confirmation.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It stops when secret suspects exist, reports only paths and kinds, and requires removal and rotation.

faq.question: Can it configure continuous integration?
faq.answer: It can suggest validation steps, but bootstrap does not write CI files.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It proposes module guidance only for packages with distinct rules.

faq.question: Which coding agents are supported?
faq.answer: The context supports Claude, Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, and Pi workflows.
